title: iewc-1998-world-heavyweight
label: Ian Walsh

won.source: Wins the tournament final over Aries "God of War" with a top-rope DDT at Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998) to become the promotion's first-ever World Heavyweight Champion.

how: Won by pinfall after a top-rope DDT, closing a nearly hour-long tournament final.
note: Still champion when the held record ends; a title defense against "Confident" Lawrence Williams was announced for "Summer Bash 98" (26 July 1998), a date the held record does not reach.

title: iewc-1998-juniorweight
label: Mad Goat

won.source: Defeats Jinsei Shakanuzi at Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998) to win the Juniorweight Championship.

note: Retains against Ivan Ramieus at Boston Massacre (27 June 1998); still champion when the held record ends.

title: iewc-1998-juniorweight
label: Jinsei Shakanuzi

won.source: Billed champion of record on Saturday Night Showcase (25 April 1998), where he retains against Shawn Collins in a first-round National Title Tournament match; the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

lost.source: Loses the title to Mad Goat at Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998).

note: Recorded as champion from billing; no document in the held record shows how or when he won the title.

title: iewc-1998-national
label: "2 Smooth" Setzer Van Strife

won.source: Billed champion of record at Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998), where he retains against Michael Robinson by disqualification; the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

note: Retains by disqualification over Michael Robinson at Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998, Nat Richards interference) and by countout over "Hardcore" Cary at the promotion's own final surviving broadcast (a title cannot change hands on either finish); still champion when the held record ends. A Ladder Match defense against "Heartbreaker" Steve Wallace was announced for "Summer Bash 98" (26 July 1998), a date the held record does not reach.

title: iewc-1998-tag-team
label: Perfectly Perfect Duo

won.source: Defeats The EOA on Saturday Night Showcase (25 April 1998) to become the promotion's first-ever World Tag Team Champions, after the previous champions-elect (The Enforcers) were released from the roster.

how: Won by pinfall in the promotion's own inaugural Tag Team Title match.

lost.source: Loses the titles to Teen Angst at Boston Massacre (27 June 1998) after a distraction by Vedder's tag partner Cobain and a controlled pinfall.

note: Retains against Teen Angst by double countout in an interim defense at Spring Fest 98 (31 May 1998).

title: iewc-1998-tag-team
label: Teen Angst

won.source: Defeats the Perfectly Perfect Duo at Boston Massacre (27 June 1998) to win the World Tag Team Championship.

how: Won by pinfall after a distraction ringing the timekeeper's bell.
note: Retains against Rod Renson and Andrew "Flash" Tucker at the promotion's own final surviving broadcast; still champions when the held record ends.
